extracted.intended_audience: newsroom staff: photojournalists, photographers, photo editors, designers, and newsroom leadership
extracted.subtask_description: A compilation of editorial standards and ethics governing the capture, editing, labeling, publication, and acceptance of photographic images in news and online community contexts. Covers what manipulations are allowed, how illustrations/posed images must be labeled, verification and provenance checks, and behavioral/professional expectations for photographers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accurate and comprehensive in the representation of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver error-free, verifiable representations across media platforms; correct errors promptly and prominently; avoid oversimplifying or highlighting incidents out of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter photographic content
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of a photograph will NEVER be changed or manipulated in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing may be added, removed, moved, reversed, distorted or otherwise altered in news/documentary photographs (repeated across AP, NYT, Journal News, many others). Exceptions are narrowly defined and must be approved and disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit edits to traditional darkroom norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the established norms of standard photo printing methods such as burning, dodging, toning and cropping are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital adjustments analogous to darkroom techniques are allowed to ensure faithful reproduction; exaggerated use of burning/dodging/sharpening/color saturation is not permitted; retouching limited to removal of scratches/dust spots and technical defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: No adding or removing objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add, remove, move, combine or otherwise alter objects or people in a news photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prohibition on inserting/excising elements, creating composites that appear documentary, or creating misleading montages; any exception must be clearly labeled and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo illustrations must be labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: When photographs are staged, manipulated or used as illustrations they must be clearly labeled as 'photo illustration' or similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photo illustrations must be obvious to the reader and never intended to deceive; captions/cutlines should explain special effects when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not stage or recreate news events
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers should not set up, re-create, direct, re-enact or otherwise manipulate subjects to make a scene appear 'found' or spontaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posing is allowed for portraits, fashion, studio work, or clearly labeled illustrations; for news, staging undermines credibility and is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal color correction with disclosure if abnormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Color correction should always be minimal and aimed at honest reproduction; cases of abnormal color or tonality should be stated in the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct color to ensure faithful reproduction; do not change the actual color content of documentary photos; major colorization must be labeled as illustrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not 'flop' (mirror) photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not flip or mirror ('flop') documentary images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flopping images is explicitly disallowed because it can misrepresent orientation/meaning; if layout requires special handling consult editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cloning/rubber stamp only for imperfection removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Cloning (Photoshop rubber stamp) can only be used to remove dust, scratches or other imperfections and not to alter content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any cloning that changes content or background requires specific approval and labeling as illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and archive originals
rubrics_metrics.description: All original digital images must be preserved/downloaded into archive or editing systems for editing or review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transmitting on location, originals should be downloaded upon return; printouts for editing must be from original camera files so provenance and review are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult editors on doubtful cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When questions arise about manipulation, color, reproduction or labeling, consult a senior/photo editor or managing editor immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any exceptions or proposals for altering photos should be escalated to higher editorial levels; decisions on sensitive or ambiguous images should involve appropriate editorial teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity of photographic context
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing should maintain the integrity of the photographic image's content and context and not misrepresent subjects or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions and credits cannot be used to correct misimpressions left by an image; avoid cropping/shooting angles that misrepresent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label reenactments and staged content
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged events; if reenactment is necessary it must be labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit labeling ensures readers know when an image is not documentary; this applies to dramatic reconstructions and staged demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo publication should not mislead readers
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not try to fool the reader; images must not be used in ways that confuse or misrepresent reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (type in photo, silhouettes, mortising) should be sparing and reviewed; suspicions about deception should be elevated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different rules for illustrations/studio/advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo illustrations, fashion, food, studio work, advertising and controlled shoots follow different guidelines and must be labeled or be obvious departures from reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such images may be manipulated artistically but must not be presented as documentary news photography; advertising photos often require editorial approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not manipulate subjects during capture
rubrics_metrics.description: While photographing, do not intentionally contribute to, alter, or seek to influence events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers should not mislead subjects to obtain photos, break laws to obtain images, or promise access without approval; portraits are an exception if clearly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and protect vulnerable subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat all subjects with respect and dignity; give special consideration to vulnerable subjects and compassion to victims of crime or tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intrude on private grief only when public has an overriding and justifiable need to see; weigh community sensibilities against news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and provenance checks for handouts and UGC
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo editors must verify the authenticity of handout photos and user-generated content and take reasonable steps to validate documentary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not automatically assume UGC is accurate; corroborate claims, validate digital material, seek consents and apply the same editorial scrutiny as other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute content and honor copyrights; credit lines should identify the source of photos, especially handouts and historical images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt include source credit; provenance helps readers assess authenticity and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept gifts, favors, compensation or pay sources/subjects for information or participation when it could influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers should avoid political, civic or business involvements that compromise or give appearance of compromising journalistic independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sabotage other journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not intentionally sabotage the efforts of other journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional behavior and cooperation among news media professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial approval required for significant manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any substantial electronic or darkroom manipulation beyond normal reproduction corrections requires approval by photo editors or senior editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulations that change content, create composite illustrations, place type on photos, create cutouts or COBs, or materially alter background must be approved and labeled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceptive cropping and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not crop or frame images in ways that would mislead readers about the event depicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers and designers should avoid shooting/cropping that misrepresents the content; consult editors if cropping could alter meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use manipulations only for faithful reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic manipulation may be used only to enhance technical quality so the image reflects what the photographer actually saw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed adjustments: contrast, exposure, gray scale, tone, minimal sharpening, dust/scratch spotting and color balancing—only insofar as they do not change reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label altered/fictional imagery clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: If technology is used to create fictional or interpretive imagery, it must be clearly evident to the reader that it is not a record of real events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a caption is necessary to explain the content is not real, the image should not be used; complex graphics and renderings should be labeled 'photo illustration' or 'graphic'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle sensitive or graphic images with editorial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing photographs of a sensitive nature (graphic content, nudity, exaggerated grief) requires discussion with photo/management editors and possibly inclusion of diversity/cultural advisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider community standards and the feelings of photo subjects; expand review group for particularly sensitive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotypes; strive for inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping individuals and groups; coverage should represent diverse viewpoints and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek diversity in subjects and viewpoints over time; be vigilant in combating prejudice in reporting, editing, presentation and hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish manipulated reader-contributed images without checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Material supplied by the public should not be put directly on air or online without adequate editorial scrutiny, verification and consent checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure resources to check facts and authenticity; in breaking news there may be tight turnaround but risks must be managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Montages and collages must not be presented as documentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographic collages, montages or composited images are acceptable only when clearly labeled and used for illustrative or interpretive purposes, not news documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use limited to interpretive stories and must be approved by photo/editors; should not be used in regular news reporting without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation through headlines, teasers, or visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines, news teases, photos, video, audio, graphics and quotes must not misrepresent or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these elements do not oversimplify or distort the story; avoid misleading promotional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat reader images with same standards as staff images
rubrics_metrics.description: User-submitted or handout images should be treated with the same care as staff-shot photos regarding manipulation and reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter reader-submitted wedding/obit images; verify and preserve reproduction quality; respect their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit use of others' content without rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not upload, post, or publish photos you do not have rights to or that infringe copyrights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online community rules (Flickr, Yahoo) emphasize uploading original content and respecting copyright; newsrooms must ensure rights clearance for file/historical images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label posed portraits or studio shots when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits and studio photographs should not mislead readers into thinking they are spontaneous; captions should clarify when a subject was posed or photographed for illustrative purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in cutlines (e.g., not implying the subject was at work when present only for portrait).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo manipulations must be rare and justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo illustrations and manipulated images should be used sparingly and only when editorially necessary to convey complex or abstract subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used, they must be developed carefully with input from photographers, photo/word editors and designers and labeled to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial 'reality check' before altering
rubrics_metrics.description: Before deciding to alter a photo, ask whether readers will be confused and whether the idea should be kicked up to the next editing level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'will readers be confused?' and consult AME/photo or executive editors when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community/online content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Online community platforms prohibit uploading pornography, exploitative violent images, hate speech, copyright-infringing content, repeated duplicate uploads, and other prohibited materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community sites have specific moderation rules (e.g., iReport, Flickr, Yahoo) and removal/ban policies; flag violations and follow platform reporting processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical/file photographs requires labeling and rights check
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and file photos must be labeled as such and licensed or used only when rights permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure readers are not misled about timing/context; identify source and confirm right to use without owner agreement if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red flags and guiding questions for publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and photographers should watch for red flags (death, nudity, exaggerated grief, blood, 'too good to be true', dangerous acts, racial stereotypes) and ask guiding questions about appropriateness and news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding questions include: Is the photo appropriate to the story? Is the news value worth upsetting readers? Does it pass the 'breakfast table' test? Should it be escalated to top editors?
